text:
marta: Quick sync — we need final recommendations for how Redwood Optimize will package quant profiles for the FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ bakeoffs. Goals: clear deployable IDs, compatibility hints for runtime, and a sane versioning story.
ashish: Are we locking to one naming convention or allowing multiple flavors per model? e.g. gpt-neo-1.3b has both gptq and awq after the bakeoff.
li: Prefer a single canonical profile per quantization config + optimizer, and then let consumers pick via routing rules. Naming idea: <model>-<arch>@<quanttool>+<precision>+v<semver>  e.g. llama2-13b@awq+int8+v1
sam: +1 to canonical. Also we need the manifest to include: compatible runtime(s), expected token-delta (accuracy), perf-regime (latency/cost), and recommended deployment cohort (hosted/dedicated/private).
marta: Draft thresholds: accuracy delta <= 1.5% (task avg) => "recommended", 1.5-3% => "use-with-caveats", >3% => "do-not-deploy". These are illustrative, we should tie to eval suite and per-task deltas.
nashish: How to encode these in the package? I'd like small machine-readable fields + freeform notes for human ops.
li: Proposed minimal manifest snippet (YAML inside qpkg):
```
profile_id: "llama2-13b@awq+int8+v1"
model: "llama2-13b"
quant_tool: "awq-0.3.1"
precision: "int8"
compat_runtimes: ["redwood-runtime-v2","docker-gpu:v3"]
accuracy_delta: "task_mean:1.2, max:2.8"
quality_flag: "use-with-caveats"
perf_regime: "p95_lat=120ms @ batch=4 on A100-80GB"
recommend_deploy: "dedicated, canary-first"
notes: "works well on long context but degrades on summarization by ~2.8%"
```
sam: That looks good. Add a checksum and a consumer-facing display_name. Also include a short list of the eval suites used (e.g., "summarize_v1, instruct_eval_v2").
opsbot: CI: qpkg validation passed for profile_id=llama2-13b@awq+int8+v1 (build 4821) :white_check_mark:
marta: For Redwood Optimize UI and registry, we should show a few computed fields: unit_token_cost_estimate, expected_throughput_range, regression_risk (low/med/high). That gives customers quick tradeoffs.
li: Versioning details: semver on profile content (v1, v1.1 for minor quant-config changes, v2 for re-run with new quant-tool). Keep profile immutable; updates create new profile_id.
nashish: What about bundling multiple profiles into a cohort? e.g., ship a 2-profile bundle for failover (awq int8 + fp8 fallback). Name pattern: <bundle>-<model>-<date>-v<semver>.
sam: Agree. Bundle manifest should list primary, fallback, and automatic routing policy (latency-first/cost-first). Example routing: prefer primary, fallback if p95>200ms or error_rate>2%.
marta: Action items: li to drop a qpkg manifest template + validator rules, sam to add UI columns for unit_cost and regression_risk, ashish to sketch a rollout playbook for the three recommended cohorts (hosted/dedicated/private).
li: I'll put the template in the repo today and add a lint rule for profile_id format.
nashish: Thanks — will reuse these fields in the bakeoff report spreadsheet. :thumbsup:
marta: sweet. if any objections, raise now, else i'll lock the spec tomorrow and ping legal for export flags.
